defect.what: tests/integration/postgres/audit-schema.test.ts, test '0032 applies forward cleanly on the existing authority (no destructive migration)': the assertion pinned forward.applied to exactly [{version:31,name:isolation_profiles},{version:32,name:audit_compliance}] while the shipped migration set now also carries 0033_application_credentials and 0034_sandbox_governance — four migrations apply forward on the 0030-converged base, so the test failed on every clean PostgreSQL rail that ran the postgres integration suites. The forward.skipped inline comment and the surrounding comments (the header bullet and the forward-run block) encoded the same stale two-migration assumption.
defect.discoveryHistory: identified during the PPR-001 delivery cycle (Task 57-b); reproduced identically on clean base 9915be6 by the Lead; independently reproduced and correctly attributed by the PPR-002 worker in an isolated environment (the DEP-040 record's DEFECT-A is the earliest written record) — two-environment cross-confirmation at attribution time. Live cross-evidence (Lead, 2026-09-21): deploy:migrate --environment preview against the real Neon preview authority applied all 33 shipped migrations and converged — the production path is proven; only the test's pinned expectation was stale.
defect.reproducedHere: third independent environment, this session: on the UNMODIFIED branch (identical to base fe26d93) with ZECK_PG_TEST_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:54331/postgres, `bunx vitest run tests/integration/postgres/audit-schema.test.ts` → exit 1, Tests 1 failed | 9 passed (10); the failure is exactly forward.applied received [{31 isolation_profiles},{32 audit_compliance},{33 application_credentials},{34 sandbox_governance}] vs the pinned two-entry list (the diff names application_credentials 33 + sandbox_governance 34 as the unexpected rows).

fix.surface: tests/integration/postgres/audit-schema.test.ts only (plus this evidence record). The 0030-converged scratch-database harness above the assertion (loadMigrations, the <=30 base filter, baseRun, the authority seeding) is untouched; the test's intent is preserved exactly — the D-08 migrations apply forward cleanly, no destructive migration, the pre-existing authority rows intact, the audit plane works on the converged base.
fix.derivation: the expected forward set is computed from the shipped migration set at runtime: convergedHead = the head version of the base set the harness just applied (baseSet.at(-1)?.version ?? 0 — 30 today, whatever the converged head is tomorrow); expectedForward = every shipped migration with version > convergedHead, mapped to {version, name}. The assertions: expect(expectedForward.length).toBeGreaterThan(0) (not vacuous — the shipped set really carries migrations beyond the base), expect(forward.applied).toEqual(expectedForward) (order-preserving: loadMigrations sorts ascending and the runner applies in that order), and expect(forward.skipped).toBe(baseSet.length) (unchanged — it was already derived). A hard-coded list — the two entries before, a four-entry list today — would recreate the same defect at migration 0035; the derivation tracks the repository.
fix.comments: the stale two-migration comments (the file-header bullet, the forward-run block, the skipped inline note) now state the derived expectation.

notes: WHY DERIVE, NOT RE-PIN: a hard-coded four-entry list ([31,32,33,34]) would be correct today and stale at migration 0035 — the exact failure mode that broke the two-entry pin this work order retires. The derivation (shipped set beyond the converged head, with version and name) makes the test track the repository: adding 0035 requires no edit here, and the non-vacuity guard keeps the test from silently passing if the base ever swallowed the whole shipped set.

The `forward.skipped` assertion was already derived (baseSet.length) and needed no change — only its inline comment carried the stale 'exactly the two D-08 migrations' assumption; the comment now states the derived expectation.

The test's title ('0032 applies forward cleanly on the existing authority (no destructive migration)') is intentionally unchanged: it is the test's identity as quoted by the work order and the prior evidence records; the intent it names (the audit-plane migrations apply forward cleanly on the converged authority) is preserved exactly.
